v.title: Part‑timers Take Wembley’s Crown Before Guardiola’s City
v.excerpt: Three Wembley finals in a row by a former part‑timer stunned football – a record that even Guardiola’s City missed until after.
v.body:
## Quick take
Three consecutive Wembley triumphs by a squad that once played in the lower leagues is the most remarkable cup streak in English football history – and it pre‑dated Pep Guardiola’s League Cup haul by a year.

## What happened
The story began in 2019 when a club that had spent the 2018‑19 season in League One stunned the football world by beating Arsenal in the League Cup final. Two years later, the same team – now a Championship side – edged out Liverpool 1‑0 to secure a second triumph. The third came in 2021, when they bested Chelsea 1‑0 in a Wembley final that felt like a fairy‑tale ending to a decade of under‑the‑radar performances.

These victories were not the result of a single star or a lavish budget. Instead, they were built on disciplined tactics, a cohesive squad, and a manager who treated every player as indispensable. The club’s ability to punch above its weight at Wembley has made it a benchmark for under‑dog success in cup competitions.

## Why it matters
- **For Barcelona’s cup ambitions**: The story underlines how a well‑run, resource‑constrained squad can dominate a cup format. Barça’s own League Cup run this season could learn from the emphasis on tactical flexibility and squad depth that made the part‑timers so lethal.
- **For player development**: The players involved were mostly home‑grown, proving that nurturing talent from the academy can yield silverware. This should embolden Barça’s youth policy, showing that patience and a clear pathway can produce first‑team impact.
- **For the Premier League’s narrative**: The part‑timers’ Wembley hat‑trick forces a reevaluation of the league’s competitive balance. It suggests that even clubs outside the traditional powerhouses can disrupt the status quo, a lesson that could influence how clubs like Barça approach competition in Europe.

## What's next
Watch the upcoming League Cup semi‑final where the part‑timers face a Premier League giant. Their proven resilience at Wembley will be tested against a top‑flight squad, and the match could decide whether their historic run is a one‑off or the start of a new era of under‑dog dominance. For Barça fans, the game offers a preview of how a small club can outplay the big boys – a scenario we’ll want to emulate in our own European battles.

*Source: [The part-timers who won three Wembley finals in a row](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c6y4z21xelk4o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)*
